notes.claim: A centrifugal pump settles at the operating point, where its curve of head against flow crosses the system's curve.
Closing a discharge valve changes the system resistance curve.
With the discharge valve closed, a centrifugal pump builds maximum head, and the power the motor needs is at or near its minimum.
As the valve opens and flow rises, the motor's current rises (source is a pump maker's start-up guide; it covers centrifugal pumps generally).
Net positive suction head (NPSH) is the minimum absolute suction pressure needed to avoid cavitation.
Cavitation is usually unwanted because of its noise and the damage it does to blade surfaces, such as pitting.
Positive displacement pumps are normally fitted with relief valves ahead of their discharge valves, to protect the pump and its discharge pipe from overpressure.
Water boils at 100 °C at sea-level pressure, and at a lower temperature where the pressure is lower.

sources.title: Why Start a Centrifugal Pump with the Discharge Valve Closed?
sources.quote: At this no-flow condition, the pump builds maximum pressure (head), but the power required by the motor is at or near its minimum.

sources.title: Why Start a Centrifugal Pump with the Discharge Valve Closed?
sources.quote: As the flow rate increases, the motor's amperage will rise.

sources.title: Controlling the rate of flow in centrifugal pumping systems and impacts on efficiency - Pump Industry Magazine
sources.quote: Throttling on the pump discharge by closing a valve (manual or automatic) has the effect of changing the system resistance curve.

sources.title: ABOUT PUMP CURVES
sources.quote: The NPSH-value of a pump is the minimum absolute pressure that must be present at the suction side of the pump to avoid cavitation.

sources.title: Examples of Cavitation and Cavitation Damage
sources.quote: Cavitation is usually undesirable because of the noise and the damage that it does to blade surfaces (pitting, etc.).

sources.title: Positive Displacement Pump Protection
sources.quote: Positive displacement pumps are normally fitted with relief valves on the upstream side of their discharge valves to protect the pump and its discharge piping from over pressurization.

sources.title: When does water boil? | Britannica
sources.quote: At sea level, atmospheric pressure is high, and water boils at 100 °C (212 °F); at higher altitudes it is lower, so water boils at a lower temperature.
